children.translated_text: <s>Mahātapā</s> said:
Formerly there was on earth a mighty great demon named <s>Andhaka</s>.
Puffed up by a boon from <s>Brahmā</s>, he brought the gods under his control.
By him all the self-possessed gods were made to abandon Mount <s>Meru</s>.
Tormented by fear of <s>Andhaka</s>, they went to <s>Brahmā</s> for refuge.
Then <s>Brahmā</s>, seeing that they had come, spoke to the best of the gods:
"Gods, what is the purpose of your coming? Tell me what is the matter."
The gods said:
"All of us gods have been oppressed by <s>Andhaka</s>, lord of the world.

children.text: trāhi sarvāṃś caturvaktra pitāmaha namo'stu te ||
children.translated_text: Protect us all, four-faced grandsire; reverence be to you."
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
"Best of the gods, I am not able to protect you from <s>Andhaka</s>.
Let us go for refuge to <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Śarva</s>, the great god.

children.text: kiṃtu pūrvaṃ mayā datto varastasya surottamāḥ
children.translated_text: But previously, best of gods, a boon was given by me to him:

children.text: avadhyastvaṃ hi bhavitā na śarīraṃ spṛśenmahīm ||
children.translated_text: 'You shall be invulnerable, and your body shall not touch the earth.'
For him, mighty as he is, the one slayer is <s>Rudra</s>, scorcher of foes.
Therefore let us all go there to the lord who dwells on <s>Kailāsa</s>."

children.text: evam uktvā yayau brahmā sadevo bhavasannidhau
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Brahmā</s> went, together with the gods, into the presence of <s>Bhava</s>.
At the sight of him, <s>Rudra</s> performed the acts beginning with rising to greet him,
and the lord of gods addressed <s>Brahmā</s>, lord of the worlds.
<s>Śambhu</s> said:

children.text: kiṃ kāryaṃ devatāḥ sarvā āgatā mama sannidhau
children.translated_text: "What business has brought all the deities into my presence?

children.text: yenāhaṃ tatkaromyāśu ājñā kāryā hi satvaram ||
children.translated_text: For whatever reason, I shall do it at once; the command must be carried out swiftly."
The gods said:
"Protect us, god, from mighty <s>Andhaka</s>, whose mind is wicked."
Just as all the gods were reporting this to the supreme lord,
at that very moment <s>Andhaka</s> arrived there with a great army.
With a fourfold force he came wishing to kill <s>Bhava</s> in battle,
and, with his retinue, desiring to abduct his wife, the daughter of the mountain.
Seeing him suddenly arriving, the assailant of the god <s>Śakra</s>,
the gods quickly armed themselves and became attendants of <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: rudro'pi vāsukiṃ dhyātvā takṣakaṃ ca dhanaṃjayam
children.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s> too, meditating on <s>Vāsuki</s>, <s>Takṣaka</s>, and <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>,
the supreme lord made them into a bracelet and a waist-cord.

children.text: nīlanāmā ca daityendro hastī bhūtvā bhavāntikam
children.translated_text: A lord of demons named <s>Nīla</s>, becoming an elephant, came near <s>Bhava</s>,
hastening there with a form as arrogant as <s>Śakra</s>'s elephant.

children.text: sa jñāto nandinā daityo vīrabhadrāya darśitaḥ
children.translated_text: That demon was recognized by <s>Nandin</s> and pointed out to <s>Vīrabhadra</s>.
<s>Vīrabhadra</s>, in the form of a lion, struck him down swiftly.
Quickly tearing off the hide of that elephant, dark like collyrium,
he offered it to <s>Rudra</s>, and he made that very hide his garment.
From then on <s>Rudra</s> became one whose cloth was an elephant-hide.
Having become clad in elephant-hide and shining with serpent ornaments,
he took up the terrible three-pointed spear and, with his hosts, pursued <s>Andhaka</s>.
Then, when the great battle of gods and demons had begun,
the world-protectors beginning with <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Skanda</s> the general,

children.text: sarve devagaṇāś cānye yuyudhuḥ samare tadā ||
children.translated_text: and all the other hosts of gods fought in the battle at that time.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā nārado yuddhaṃ yayau nārāyaṇaṃ prati
children.translated_text: Seeing that battle, <s>Nārada</s> went to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>

children.text: śaśaṃsa ca mahad yuddhaṃ kailāse dānavaiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: and reported the great battle with the demons on <s>Kailāsa</s>.
Hearing this, <s>Janārdana</s>, mounted on <s>Garuḍa</s>, took up his discus,

children.text: tamevaṃ deśam āgamya yuyudhe dānavaiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: came to that very place, and fought with the demons.

children.text: āgatya ca tato devā hariṇāpyāyitā raṇe
children.translated_text: When he arrived, the gods, though strengthened by <s>Hari</s> in battle,
all became downcast in face and intent on flight.

children.text: tatra bhagneṣu deveṣu svayaṃ rudro'ndhakaṃ yayau
children.translated_text: When the gods had been routed there, <s>Rudra</s> himself went against <s>Andhaka</s>.
There a great battle took place between them, making the hairs stand on end.
There that god struck the demon violently with his trident.
When he had been struck, whatever blood of his fell on the ground,
from it countless other <s>Andhakas</s> arose in great numbers.

children.text: tad dṛṣṭvā mahadāścaryaṃ rudraḥ śūle'ndhakaṃ mṛdhe
children.translated_text: Seeing that great marvel, <s>Rudra</s> seized <s>Andhaka</s> in battle on his spear,
and the supreme lord danced with him held on the tip of the three-pointed weapon.
All the other <s>Andhakas</s> who had arisen there
were slain by <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the supreme lord, with his discus.
But again and again, from the showers of streams of blood of the one impaled on the spear,
they arose without ceasing. Then <s>Rudra</s> became filled with anger.
From his mouth, because of his great wrath, a flame issued forth.

children.text: tadrūpadhāriṇī devī yāṃ tāṃ yogeśvarīṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: The goddess bearing that form is the one whom they know as <s>Yogeśvarī</s>.
Another, bearing his own form, was also created by <s>Viṣṇu</s>;

children.text: brahmaṇā kārttikeyena indreṇa ca yamena ca
children.translated_text: and by <s>Brahmā</s>, by <s>Kārttikeya</s>, by <s>Indra</s>, and by <s>Yama</s>,
and by the god <s>Varāha</s>, and by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the supreme lord.
He fashioned for that goddess the form that had raised up the netherworld.
And <s>Māheśvarī</s>, O king: these are the eight Mothers.
Hear the reason for which these have been declared, as determined by the knower of the field.

children.text: śarīrād devatānāṃ tu tadidaṃ kīrtitaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: This has been recounted by me as arising from the bodies of the deities.

children.text: kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobho mado moho'tha pañcamaḥ
children.translated_text: Desire, anger, greed, pride, and delusion as the fifth,
envy is said to be the sixth, slander the seventh,
and jealousy is to be known as the eighth: these are the eight Mothers.

children.text: kāmaṃ yogeśvarīṃ viddhi krodho māheśvarīṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Know desire to be <s>Yogeśvarī</s>, and anger likewise to be <s>Māheśvarī</s>.

children.text: lobhastu vaiṣṇavī proktā brahmāṇī mada eva ca ||
children.translated_text: Greed is called <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>, and pride indeed is <s>Brahmāṇī</s>.

children.text: mohaḥ svayaṃbhūḥ kaumārī mātsaryaṃ cendrajaṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: Delusion is itself <s>Kaumārī</s>, and they know envy as born of <s>Indra</s>.
The goddess who bears <s>Yama</s>'s staff is slander itself,
and jealousy is named <s>Vārāhī</s>; thus these have been proclaimed.
This group beginning with desire has been described as existing in the body.

children.text: jagrāha mūrtiṃ tu yathā tathā te kīrtitaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: How it assumed bodily form has thus been recounted to you by me.
And when his blood had been exceedingly dried up by these deities,

children.text: kṣayaṃ gatāsurī māyā sa ca siddho'ndhako'bhavat
children.translated_text: the demonic illusion perished, and that <s>Andhaka</s> became perfected.
All this <s>ātmavidyāmṛta</s> (the nectar of knowledge of the self) has been told to you by me.
Whoever constantly hears this auspicious origin of the Mothers,

children.text: tasya tāḥ sarvato rakṣāṃ kurvantyanudinaṃ nṛpa ||
children.translated_text: for him, O king, they provide protection on every side day after day.
And whoever recites this birth of the Mothers, O best of men,

children.text: sa dhanyaḥ sarvadā loke śivalokaṃ ca gacchati ||
children.translated_text: he is blessed at all times in the world, and he goes to the world of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: tāsāṃ ca brahmaṇā dattā aṣṭamī tithiruttamā
children.translated_text: And the excellent eighth lunar day was given to them by <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: etāḥ sampūjayed bhaktyā bilvāhāro naraḥ sadā
children.translated_text: A man who always worships these Mothers with devotion, living on bilva fruit,

children.text: tasya tāḥ parituṣṭāstu kṣemārogyaṃ dadanti ca ||
children.translated_text: for him they, being fully satisfied, grant security and freedom from illness.
